messages:
evan-cs: FYI — enterprise customer reported a weird combo: embeddings endpoint started returning a 422 'dimension mismatch' for some requests, tail latency spiked ~3x after they increased max_batch_size to 128, and they also saw duplicate billing lines for the same request. Repro steps below.

marta-eng: ugh, do we have their request payload & model name? which model/variant and embedding dim?

evan-cs: They were using model: text-embed-rl-1536 (customer-managed variant). Payload example: `{"input": ["doc1","doc2"], "model": "text-embed-rl-1536", "max_batch_size": 128}`. Some requests returned embeddings with length 1536, others 1538 (422). They said it started after changing max_batch_size from 64->128.

sam-oncall: Can you paste the raw request IDs/timestamps? we should correlate with dynbatch logs and billing events. Also include any Authorization failures.

evan-cs: trace_id=trc_20260315_9a7c; requests around 2026-03-15T17:00:03Z. They also reported intermittent 401 when retrying after a 422; billing shows two token entries at 17:00:04 and 17:00:06 for same client request_id.

lina-ml: Hypothesis: when max_batch_size increased we started coalescing heterogeneous requests (old clients still sending a different embedding spec / extra metadata) and dynamic batching combined incompatible pre/postprocessing, leading to an off-bytes serialization bug that produced stray padding -> wrong vector length. Also retry logic might re-submit after a transform error, creating double billing.

marta-eng: Let's get runtime logs. infra-bot, can you pull dynbatch decisions and embed runtime logs for trace_id=trc_20260315_9a7c (window ±20s)?

infra-bot: logs pulled: `/var/logs/inference/dynbatch/2026-03-15/17/trace_trc_20260315_9a7c.log` — summary attached (snippet):
```
[17:00:02.998] DEBUG dynbatch: enqueue req r=9876 sz=2 model=text-embed-rl-1536 client_schema=v1
[17:00:03.001] DEBUG dynbatch: enqueue req r=9877 sz=1 model=text-embed-rl-1536 client_schema=v2
[17:00:03.002] INFO  dynbatch: coalescing window closed, batch_size=3, max_batch_size=128
[17:00:03.003] WARN  preprocess: schema_mismatch detected between requests: client_schema=v1 vs v2
[17:00:03.004] INFO  batch_exec: selected kernel=quant_kernel_q4_1536
[17:00:03.005] ERROR postprocess: serialized_vector_length=1538 expected=1536, req=9877
[17:00:03.006] ERROR service: returning 422 to req=9877 trace=trc_20260315_9a7c
[17:00:03.007] INFO  retry: client_retries r=9877 attempt=1
[17:00:03.008] INFO  billing: charge_emitted req=9877 tokens=42 invoice_line=inv_ABC123
[17:00:03.009] INFO  billing: charge_emitted req=9877 tokens=42 invoice_line=inv_ABC124
```

sam-oncall: That looks bad — two invoice lines were created for the same failed request, and schema mismatch got through into coalescing. Why didn't schema validation block coalescing earlier? Dynbatch should group only compatible schemas.

lina-ml: Possible race: schema checks run per-request but there is a micro-window where coalesce picks up requests while schema tag update hasn't propagated from preprocessor thread. Also I see batch_exec selected a quantization kernel assuming 1536; if a request had a different preproc (v2) we could end up writing an extra 2 bytes of metadata into the vector buffer.

marta-eng: Repro plan: 1) reproduce locally with max_batch_size=128 and two clients sending different client_schema tags; 2) enable strict_schema=true in the API layer to force early rejection; 3) temporarily set max_batch_size back to 64 for customer; 4) patch billing to dedupe charges for requests that fail with postprocess errors and have same trace_id within 10s.

evan-cs: Customer wants a mitigation now. They can flip back to 64 but they'd prefer a hotfix since they need throughput. They also asked for a reproducible client script so they can validate after fixes.

sam-oncall: I'll push a quick guard: if preprocess detects mixed client_schema in a pending window, emit `coalesce_skip=true` and flush smaller compatible sub-batches. That should avoid mixing incompatible preps. Roll to canary in staging and then prod.

marta-eng: Also add a hard early validation step: before coalesce finalize, assert expected_vector_len == model_dim, if mismatch -> return 422 immediately without emitting billing event. Billing should only emit on success path. File a billing ticket to reverse inv_ABC124 for the customer.

billing-bot: billing ticket created: BT-6123 (refund request for inv_ABC124). Noted customer and support ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/5691

lina-ml: For repro, here's a minimal python snippet (customer-facing) to trigger mismatch locally — they need to send two concurrent requests with slightly different preproc flags:

```
# repro_mismatch.py
import requests
from threading import Thread

def req(schema_flag):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={
        'model': 'text-embed-rl-1536',
        'input': ['a'*100],
        'client_schema': schema_flag,
        'max_batch_size': 128
    }, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer XXX'})
    print(schema_flag, r.status_code, r.text)

threads = [Thread(target=req, args=(f'v{i}',)) for i in (1,2)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```

marta-eng: Good. I'll open a PR to add `coalesce_skip` logic + early-length-assert. sam-oncall will coordinate canary. Lina will add unit test that simulates weird padding.

sam-oncall: Timeline: quick patch (1 day) to gate coalescing and billing fix (1 day) to avoid double charge. Will contact customer with mitigation steps: revert max_batch_size or enable strict_schema, and inform we've created BT-6123 for refund.

evan-cs: Customer was satisfied with rollback path and wants updates. I'll send a support update and link to the staging repro. Thanks team :thumbsup:

marta-eng: Add follow-ups: - ensure dynbatch has stronger per-request schema tag atomics - add monitoring alert when postprocess errors >0.1% in 1m - ensure billing emit is idempotent keyed by trace_id+req_id

infra-bot: follow-up tasks created: INFRA-2048, RUNTIME-8113, BILLING-4321

sam-oncall: I'll post once canary is healthy. If anyone sees similar traces, ping me with trace id.

evan-cs: closing loop with customer now.
